title_en: The Trial of the Father of the Atomic Bomb
english_paragraphs: J. Robert Oppenheimer, born in New York on 22 April 1904, was an accomplished physicist and prominent lecturer at Berkeley and Caltech. From April 1943 he oversaw a secretive weapons installation at Los Alamos, whose bombs were the collaborative creation of a thousands-strong workforce.

In the pre-dawn darkness of 16 July 1945, the first nuclear test illuminated the desolate New Mexico landscape with a blinding glare, its explosive force roughly 20 kilotons. On 6 and 9 August 1945 atomic bombings devastated Hiroshima and Nagasaki, where year-end fatalities numbered well over 100,000 and about 70,000 respectively.

Oppenheimer left Los Alamos in October 1945 and from 1947 presided over Princeton's Institute for Advanced Study. In October 1949 the advisory committee he chaired, expressing misgivings, unanimously counselled against a crash programme for the hydrogen bomb, a vastly more destructive weapon. In December 1953 a presidential directive severed his access to confidential documentation.

From 12 April to 6 May 1954 he was cross-examined at a security hearing, an administrative proceeding, not a criminal prosecution. On 29 June 1954 the Atomic Energy Commission voted 4 to 1 against letting him regain his clearance, two days before his consultancy contract was due to expire. The ruling did not find him disloyal, but nonetheless questioned his character and associates.

On 2 December 1963 President Johnson bestowed on him the Fermi Award, which Kennedy had authorised before his assassination. Oppenheimer died on 18 February 1967. In December 2022 the energy secretary officially vacated the 1954 determination, calling the process flawed and contrary to the commission's rules. The stigma of the revocation had persisted for fifty-five years beyond his lifetime.
chinese_source_paragraphs: J·罗伯特·奥本海默1904年4月22日生于纽约，是一位**卓有成就的**(accomplished)物理学家，也是伯克利和加州理工学院的**知名**(prominent)**教师**(lecturer)。从1943年4月起，他**主管**(oversaw)洛斯阿拉莫斯的一处**秘密**(secretive)武器**设施**(installation)；这里的**炸弹**(bombs)是**数千人的**(thousands-strong)**劳动力**(workforce)**共同协作的**(collaborative)**创造成果**(creation)。

1945年7月16日**黎明前的**(pre-dawn)黑暗中，第一次核试验以一道**刺眼的强光**(blinding glare)**照亮了**(illuminated)新墨西哥州**荒凉的**(desolate)**景观**(landscape)，其**爆炸**(explosive)威力约合2万吨TNT当量。1945年8月6日和9日，原子弹**轰炸**(bombings)**摧毁了**(devastated)广岛和长崎，在这两地，**年底的**(year-end)**死亡人数**(fatalities)**分别**(respectively)达到了远超十万和约七万。

1945年10月，**奥本海默**(Oppenheimer)离开洛斯阿拉莫斯；从1947年起，他**掌管/执掌**(presided over)普林斯顿高等研究院。1949年10月，他担任主席的**顾问**(advisory)委员会表达了**疑虑**(misgivings)，并**一致**(unanimously)**建议拒绝**(counselled against)一项针对**氢**(hydrogen)弹的**紧急计划**(crash programme)，一种**极其**(vastly)更加具有**毁灭性的**(destructive)武器。1953年12月，一道**总统的**(presidential)**指令**(directive)**切断了**(severed)他**接触**(access to)**机密**(confidential)**文件**(documentation)**的权限**(access to)。

1954年4月12日至5月6日，他在一场安全**听证会**(hearing)上接受**盘问**(cross-examined)，这场听证会是**行政的**(administrative)**程序**(proceeding)，而非刑事的**起诉**(prosecution)。1954年6月29日，**原子能**(Atomic Energy)委员会以4比1投票反对让他**恢复**(regain)**安全许可**(clearance)，在他的**咨询**(consultancy)合同预计要**到期**(expire)之前，还剩两天。裁决没有认定他**不忠**(disloyal)，但**仍然**(nonetheless)质疑了他的品格和他所**结交的人**(associates)。

1963年12月2日，约翰逊总统**授予**(bestowed on)他费米奖，该奖项是肯尼迪在**遇刺**(assassination)前**批准**(authorised)的。奥本海默于1967年2月18日去世。2022年12月，能源**部长**(secretary)**正式**(officially)**撤销了**(vacated)1954年的**裁定**(determination)，称当年的程序是**有缺陷的**(flawed)且**违背了**(contrary to)委员会的规定。**撤销**(revocation)安全许可带来的**污名**(stigma)，在他的**一生**(lifetime)结束之后，又**持续了**(persisted)五十五年。

sentences.chinese_source: 1954年4月12日至5月6日，他在一场安全**听证会**(hearing)上接受**盘问**(cross-examined)，这场听证会是**行政的**(administrative)**程序**(proceeding)，而非刑事的**起诉**(prosecution)。

sentences.english: On 29 June 1954 the Atomic Energy Commission voted 4 to 1 against letting him regain his clearance, two days before his consultancy contract was due to expire.
sentences.chinese_source: 1954年6月29日，**原子能**(Atomic Energy)委员会以4比1投票反对让他**恢复**(regain)**安全许可**(clearance)，在他的**咨询**(consultancy)合同预计要**到期**(expire)之前，还剩两天。

sentences.english: The ruling did not find him disloyal, but nonetheless questioned his character and associates.
sentences.chinese_source: 裁决没有认定他**不忠**(disloyal)，但**仍然**(nonetheless)质疑了他的品格和他所**结交的人**(associates)。

sentences.english: On 2 December 1963 President Johnson bestowed on him the Fermi Award, which Kennedy had authorised before his assassination.
sentences.chinese_source: 1963年12月2日，约翰逊总统**授予**(bestowed on)他费米奖，该奖项是肯尼迪在**遇刺**(assassination)前**批准**(authorised)的。
奥本海默于1967年2月18日去世。

sentences.english: In December 2022 the energy secretary officially vacated the 1954 determination, calling the process flawed and contrary to the commission's rules.
sentences.chinese_source: 2022年12月，能源**部长**(secretary)**正式**(officially)**撤销了**(vacated)1954年的**裁定**(determination)，称当年的程序是**有缺陷的**(flawed)且**违背了**(contrary to)委员会的规定。

sentences.english: The stigma of the revocation had persisted for fifty-five years beyond his lifetime.
sentences.chinese_source: **撤销**(revocation)安全许可带来的**污名**(stigma)，在他的**一生**(lifetime)结束之后，又**持续了**(persisted)五十五年。

approved_summary: 物理学家奥本海默领导数千人造出原子弹，1945年完成首次核试验，随后原子弹用于轰炸广岛、长崎。
战后，他主持的顾问委员会一致反对紧急推进氢弹计划；氢弹是一种比原子弹破坏力更强的核武器。
1954年他接受安全听证，这是行政审查，并非刑事起诉；裁定也未认定他不忠。
原子能委员会以4比1拒绝恢复他接触机密资料的资格，质疑其品格和交往，使其背负污名。
1963年虽获费米奖，1954年裁定直到2022年才由能源部长以程序违规为由撤销，距他去世已55年。
